items.item_text: Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
Certification in the field of ergonomics from a nationally recognized accreditation body such as the BCPE (i.e., CPE or AEP)
Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, public health, or similar discipline or equivalent combination of education and work experience of at least five years
Master's degree or equivalent combination of education and work experience in a clinical field related to human factor analysis.

Knowledge and experience applying ergonomic principles and methods to evaluate and control occupational health stressors, including assessing repetitive motion injuries and musculoskeletal risks across diverse work environments and recommending corrective actions to reduce injuries and illnesses.
Experience utilizing job analysis in the causation determination of occupational claims.
Experience developing and delivering environmental health and safety training to adult learners from diverse backgrounds, job classifications, and educational levels.
Experience with conducting in-service training and education programs within area of expertise.
Experience conducting workplace assessments, audits, investigations, and evaluations; identifying hazards and compliance issues; and implementing or coordinating timely corrective actions.
Experience with understanding and interpreting drawings, specifications and campus standards
Experience collaborating with Workers’ Compensation, medical, or disability management professionals on ergonomic claims management and injury prevention.

Under the general direction of the Medical Director, this position manages the Ergonomics program for the campus and helps ensure that campus policies and state regulations are complied with to achieve a safe environment for staff, faculty and student employees. Serves as subject matter expert, develops and implements training, and collaborates with Department Safety Coordinators (DSCs) and others to promote and support ergonomic solutions. This position will develop and recommend improvements to processes in all areas of responsibility through objective data collection, analysis and focused practical and feasible solutions.

Working knowledge of federal and state occupational health and safety regulations, including the ability to interpret new and existing requirements, determine their applicability to campus operations, and develop strategies and procedures to achieve compliance.

Strong oral and written communication, presentation, interpersonal, and technical writing skills, including preparing detailed compliance reports and professional correspondence; developing institutional policies and procedures for an integrated ergonomics program; and proficiency with word processing and spreadsheet applications.
